answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: A mine operator must immediately contact MSHA within 15 minutes (using the toll-free number 1-800-746-1553) once the operator knows or should know that a death of an individual at the mine has occurred.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA within 15 minutes at the toll-free number once it knows or should know an accident involving death occurred.
claims.quote:
The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

(a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where no methane is present in the ventilating current, the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust in all underground areas of a coal mine must be maintained so that its incombustible content is not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent where rock dust is required.
claims.quote: it shall be distributed upon the top, floor, and sides of all underground areas of a coal mine and maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: This 80 percent baseline applies specifically in the absence of methane; the requirement increases only when methane is present.
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: Under 30 CFR § 75.1714(a), each operator must make available to every miner who goes underground (and to authorized visitors) an approved self-rescue device that is adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer. Section 75.1714-1 clarifies this can be met by a 1-hour SCSR, an SCSR of at least 10 minutes combined with a 1-hour canister, or another approved self-contained breathing apparatus providing at least 1 hour of protection.

claims.text: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect that person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer

claims.text: The 1-hour requirement can be satisfied by a 1-hour SCSR, an SCSR of at least 10 minutes combined with a 1-hour canister, or another approved apparatus providing 1 hour or more of protection.
claims.quote: A 1-hour SCSR; (b) A SCSR of not less than 10 minutes and a 1-hour canister; or (c) Any other self-contained breathing apparatus which provides protection for a period of 1 hour or longer

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Under 30 CFR § 57.4361, underground metal/nonmetal mines must hold evacuation drills at least once every six months.

claims.text: Evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties. This training must be conducted in conditions that as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 of those 40 hours must be given at the minesite.

claims.text: A new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Training shall be conducted in conditions that as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 hours shall be given at the minesite.
claims.quote: Such training shall be conducted in conditions which as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level (PEL) for noise at a mine is a time-weighted average over 8 hours (TWA8) of 90 dBA — equivalently, a noise dose of 100% — integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA. The mine operator must assure no miner is exposed during any work shift to noise exceeding this level; if exposure exceeds it, the operator must use all feasible engineering and administrative controls to reduce exposure to the PEL and enroll the miner in a hearing conservation program. Additionally, no miner may ever be exposed to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA (unadjusted for hearing protectors).

claims.text: Permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, or equivalently a dose of 100%, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

claims.text: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed during any work shift to noise exceeding the permissible exposure level, and if exceeded must use all feasible engineering and administrative controls and enroll the miner in a hearing conservation program.
claims.quote: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed during any work shift to noise that exceeds the permissible exposure level. If during any work shift a miner's noise exposure exceeds the permissible exposure level, the mine operator must use all feasible engineering and administrative controls to reduce the miner's noise exposure to the permissible exposure level, and enroll the miner in a hearing conservation program that complies with § 62.150 of this part.

claims.text: No miner may be exposed at any time to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA, unadjusted for hearing protector use.
claims.quote: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed at any time to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA, as determined without adjustment for the use of any hearing protector.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: At metal and nonmetal mines (governed by 30 CFR § 56.9300), berms or guardrails on the banks of roadways must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air in an approved refuge alternative must sustain each person for 96 hours.

claims.text: Breathable air mechanisms must sustain each person for 96 hours
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not contain any information about FAA drone certification. They only cover MSHA (Mine Safety and Health Administration) regulations under 30 CFR, including site-specific hazard awareness training (46.11), mine map certification by state-registered engineers/surveyors (75.1201, 77.1201), and certified person requirements for mine foremen/examiners (75.100). None of these address FAA requirements for piloting drones over mine sites, so I cannot answer this question from the given material.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not contain any information about EPA stormwater discharge permits. They only cover 30 CFR §§ 75.1716, 75.1716-2 through 75.1716-4, and 75.1717, which deal with permits required from the Coal Mine Safety District Manager (under the Secretary of Labor/MSHA framework) for mining operations conducted under rivers, streams, lakes, or other bodies of water—not with stormwater runoff or EPA permitting requirements.
